# What the TOOLS image is allowed to install from PyPI, by version AND by bytes
# (#1734, SEC-E2A). `Dockerfile` installs this as root at image build, and that
# image is published publicly, rebuilt daily, and is the trust root of every
# scan this project runs against someone else's repository. A resolver reaching
# PyPI for the other 88 lines below would run an attacker-chosen release's
# install-time code with full privileges inside it.
#
# `pip install --require-hashes --no-deps -r` this file: --require-hashes makes
# pip refuse any artifact whose digest is not written down here, and --no-deps
# makes THIS FILE the complete list rather than a starting point for a
# resolver. That is why the whole closure is spelled out and not just the three
# tools: with --no-deps pip installs exactly these lines, so a closure missing
# one fails loudly at the first import instead of silently resolving something
# unpinned.
#
# The closure was resolved with `uv pip compile --generate-hashes
# --python-version 3.12` for BOTH linux targets docker-publish.yml builds
# (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu); the two resolve to
# an identical 91-pin set. `uv pip compile --universal` adds exactly one more,
# pywin32, behind `sys_platform == 'win32'` -- a marker `bump_pins.py` does not
# carry through a rewrite, so the linux resolution is what is committed. See
# DEVELOPMENT.md, "Regenerating the pinned dependency hashes".
#
# The digests are not written by hand. `python3 devtools/bump_pins.py
# requirements --file requirements-tools.txt --write` reads each one from
# PyPI's JSON API and recomputes it from the downloaded wheel. Both linux
# architectures' wheels are pinned on every line, because pip on the arm64 leg
# of the publish fetches a different artifact than pip on the amd64 leg and
# needs its digest present.

# The three tools the image exists to ship. Each is ALSO pinned by an `ARG
# <NAME>_VERSION` in the Dockerfile, where the version is visible beside the
# tool it belongs to; `tests/test_dockerfile.py` fails if the two disagree, so
# neither can be bumped alone.
